business_problem: Yile Technology needed to replace an RDBMS that produced multi-second game response times and could not support rapid global scaling.
solution_summary: Yile Technology rebuilt the data layer behind its social casino games on MongoDB Atlas after an early relational prototype proved too slow even with small player counts. Atlas became the store for player status, prior behavior, and operational game data, which better fit a document model than rigid rows and columns and could be migrated in about a month. By removing database administration burden and giving the team an easier way to evolve schemas, Atlas let developers focus on gameplay optimization and global launches instead of firefighting the backend. The result was a dramatic drop in response time, faster scaling, and a stronger player experience as Yile expanded its titles internationally.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores player profile, behavior, and operational game data for Yile's online gaming services.

data_flow: Player profile, behavior, and operational game data is written to MongoDB Atlas and served back to gaming services in real time so sessions stay responsive as traffic scales.
business_outcome: Yile dropped response times from 3 seconds to below 0.5 seconds, scaled its games globally, and freed engineers from database firefighting.
metrics: By August 2021, Online808 had more than 1 million members.
Even when there were as few as 50 players connected to the game at the same time, the game response time could be as long as 3 seconds.
On the second round of the internal pressure test, the game's responsive time improved significantly to well below the required 0.5 seconds, a more than 6x improvement.
architecture_clues: All customer profile data, including player status and previous behavior, moved from the relational database to MongoDB.
MongoDB Atlas removed much of the basic operational maintenance load from the team.
The data model supports fast schema changes for rapidly evolving game features.
evidence_quotes: Within a month, we had completely replaced the RDBMS and all customer profile data was stored on MongoDB, this included player status and previous behavior as well as some of the game's operational data.
Even when there were as few as 50 players connected to the game at the same time, the game response time could be as long as 3 seconds.
On the second round of the internal pressure test, the game's responsive time improved significantly to well below the required 0.5 seconds, a more than 6x improvement.
